title: Samsu-iluna's reign
dateNote: Approximate reign dates in the average chronology; not a lifespan.

sentences.text: Samsu-iluna reigned approximately 1749–1712 BCE in the average chronology.
He was one of Hammu-rabi’s successors.

relationships.label: Babylon reference during reign; rule relationship requires direct corroboration

gaps: A source directly stating Samsu-iluna ruled Babylon was not inspected within the page ceiling; the city association is a reference point only and does not establish personal presence or residence.

title: Rim-Sin I's reign
dateNote: Approximate reign dates as given by the French Ministry of Culture; identified as Rim-Sin I from the Larsa dynasty and early second-millennium context. The inspected page does not separately discuss Rim-Sin II.

sentences.text: Rim-Sin I ruled Larsa approximately 1822–1763 BCE.
Babylon under Hammurabi took Larsa in 1763 BCE, ending his rule there.

gaps: Required Larsa reference coordinates are missing: the inspected geographical source identifies Tell es Senkereh and its relative setting but has no numeric coordinates. A numeric point cannot be added without inspecting an appropriate coordinate source.

title: Larsa
dateNote: Editorial research window aligned to the Met’s title span for the Isin-Larsa and Old Babylonian periods; it is not a city lifespan or sourced continuous occupation interval.

sentences.text: The French Ministry of Culture identifies Tell es Senkereh as ancient Larsa and places it in the Lower Mesopotamian plain between the Tigris and Euphrates.
The Met period dates are used only as an explicitly editorial study window for this entry.

gaps: Required numeric site-reference coordinates are absent from the inspected French Ministry descriptions. The assignment’s required map point is therefore missing; no location was inferred from the place name.
